title: Section 131 — Punishment for assault or criminal force otherwise than on grave provocation

content.overview: BNS s. 131 — Punishment for assault or criminal force otherwise than on grave provocation.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Punishment for assault or criminal force otherwise than on grave provocation. BNS restatement of IPC 352. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 352. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 131 is the rule on “Punishment for assault or criminal force otherwise than on grave provocation”. The section provides that whoever assaults or uses criminal force to any person otherwise than on grave and sudden provocation given by that person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 131 exists so that “Punishment for assault or criminal force otherwise than on grave provocation” has a closed legal test in Chapter VI — Of Offences Affecting the Human Body. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Homicide, organised crime, terrorism, hurt, acid, restraint, assault, kidnapping and trafficking.

The provision in detail
131. Whoever assaults or uses criminal force to any person otherwise than on grave and sudden provocation given by that person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both

Essential ingredients
1. Whoever assaults or uses criminal force to any person otherwise than on grave and sudden provocation given by that person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both

Explanations
Explanation 1.—Grave and sudden provocation will not mitigate the punishment for an offence under this section,—

(a) if the provocation is sought or voluntarily provoked by the offender as an excuse for the offence; or

(b) if the provocation is given by anything done in obedience to the law, or by a public servant, in the lawful exercise of the powers of such public servant; or

(c) if the provocation is given by anything done in the lawful exercise of the right of private defence

Explanation 2.—Whether the provocation was grave and sudden enough to mitigate the offence, is a question of fact

learningObjectives: Master the baseline punishment for assault or criminal force under BNS s. 131.
Understand the punishment tier: imprisonment up to three months, fine up to ₹2,500, or both.
Analyze Explanation 1 setting out the three disqualifying conditions for grave provocation.
Examine Explanation 2 providing that provocation is a question of fact.
enhancement.definition: BNS s. 131 establishes the general baseline punishment for assault or criminal force: whoever assaults or uses criminal force to any person otherwise than on grave and sudden provocation given by that person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to two thousand five hundred rupees, or with both.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Establishes a baseline summary punishment for unprovoked threats and applications of minor physical force that fall short of causing bodily hurt.
statutoryFramework: Chapter VI — Of Offences Affecting the Human Body, BNS s. 131 (corresponding to IPC s. 352).
Offences punished: Assault (s. 130) or Criminal Force (s. 129).
Condition: Committed otherwise than on grave and sudden provocation.
Punishment: Imprisonment of either description up to three months, or fine up to ₹2,500, or both (fine modernized from ₹500 under IPC 352).
Explanation 1: Provocation will not mitigate if sought as an excuse, done in obedience to law, or in lawful private defence.
Explanation 2: Whether the provocation was grave and sudden enough to mitigate is a question of fact.
essentialIngredients: The accused committed an assault (Section 130) OR used criminal force (Section 129).
The act was committed against a person.
The act was committed otherwise than on grave and sudden provocation given by that person.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 131 is the general charging provision for simple assault and simple criminal force. Where an individual threatens someone with a gesture or applies non-consensual force that causes fear or annoyance, but does NOT cause actual bodily pain (hurt) and does not fall under specialized aggravated categories (such as assaulting a public servant or outraging modesty), Section 131 provides the penalty. The punishment extends up to three months imprisonment, a fine up to ₹2,500, or both. Explanation 1 imports the standard three provisos from homicide law: provocation cannot be claimed if the accused voluntarily provoked it as an excuse, if it arose from a public servant acting lawfully, or if it arose from someone exercising lawful private defence. Explanation 2 confirms that whether provocation was grave and sudden is always a factual determination for the court.
examples: Teaching example (Unprovoked shove): An individual pushes a customer out of a ticket queue without causing pain or injury, purely to skip the line. This is using criminal force unprovoked, punishable under s. 131.
Teaching example (Brandishing a stick): An accused brandishes a stick in a neighbor's face unprovoked, threatening to strike him. This is simple assault under s. 131.
distinctions: Section 131 vs Section 115 (Voluntarily Causing Hurt): Section 131 applies when no bodily pain/injury ensues (up to 3 months); Section 115 applies when hurt is caused (up to 1 year).
Section 131 vs Section 136: Section 131 applies to unprovoked assaults; Section 136 applies to assaults committed on grave and sudden provocation (punishing with up to 1 month).
problemApplication: Issue: Whether an accused who spat on a pedestrian's coat after a verbal disagreement is punishable under s. 131.
Rule: Spitting on someone's clothing constitutes using criminal force to cause annoyance without consent under BNS s. 129, punishable under s. 131.
Application: Force was applied by disposing a substance, causing annoyance, without grave provocation.
Conclusion: The accused is guilty under BNS s. 131.
